prompt: In a right triangle, the side opposite angle $\theta$ has length $12$ and the side adjacent to $\theta$ has length $5$. What is the value of $\tan\theta$? Give your answer as a decimal.
hint: TOA: tangent is opposite over adjacent.

hints.text: TOA: tangent is opposite over adjacent.

learningObjective: Compute a tangent ratio in a right triangle.
explanation: The hypotenuse here would be $13$ — this is a $5$-$12$-$13$ triangle.
Note that tangent, unlike sine and cosine, can exceed $1$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Range as a sanity check
steps: Sine and cosine are always between $-1$ and $1$, because the hypotenuse is the longest side.
Tangent has no such bound — it can be any real number.
So a sine answer above $1$ is definitely wrong, but a tangent above $1$ is perfectly ordinary.
